data.narrative:
QuantumDiamonds is a seed-stage quantum computing company founded by Kevin Berghoff and Fleming Bruckmaier. The quantum computing sector comprises 3 public peers (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private competitors including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

The valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method due to peer-set constraints. The Stage-Progression method applies a 2.5x multiplier to the $7M seed round as a proxy for current value, implying $18M. A peer-median approach is not applicable: while 8 quantum computing peers exist in the dataset, none meet the narrow filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables—the minimum three-datapoint threshold was not satisfied. Peer-median calibration would therefore require broadening to all-sector data, introducing unacceptable noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M (low) to $20M (median $18M). This reflects conservative application of stage-progression mechanics with ±15% variance bounds. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer validation; the quantum computing sector's wide dispersion in business models and maturity stages limits traditional comparable-company inference. The $152M facility commitment signals substantial non-dilutive capital availability, but does not mechanically support valuation without clarity on drawdown terms and operational milestones. Additional data on burn rate, customer traction, or IP defensibility would strengthen confidence in this range.
